title: extcap: Support logging via control pipe in extcap-base
description:
In extcap-base, supporting recognizing the control pipe arguments,
    and opening the control pipes if set. If the control out pipe is
    available, then send logging through it. Use a custom logger for
    this purpose, which requires that extcaps using extcap-base pass
    the extcap parameters object when initializing logging.
    
Also read SP_QUIT and SP_TOOLBAR_CTRL messages from the control in
    pipe, calling callbacks if registered (using the existing graceful
    shutdown callback for SP_QUIT).
    
extcap-base processes its arguments at the end, after an individual
    extcap takes first crack tat them, so any existing extcaps that use
    extcap-base and already handle the control pipe arguments will see no
    effect. Note that none of the extcaps in the repo do so, as they don't
    support the control pipes yet, so this has no immediate effect. It
    establishes a framework to deal with #17131 later.

notes.body: The disadvantage of using the (always set up) stdout for this is that an extcap can be run in capture mode from the command line, in which case we wouldn't want to do this. So it might make sense to only redirect when we know we have another pipe, e.g. !26093

Cool PR ! Just FYI, once you'll be done, please feel free to remove this function. This was a workaround and doesn't make much sense if you manage to properly implement graceful shutdown on Windows.

Thanks for pointing that out.

For backwards compatibility, I expect I may need to have extcaps indicate in their configuration whether or not they're prepared to open the control pipes and receive messages, and fallback to the other method if they're not. That might mean keeping this function and calling it for extcaps that didn't get the message.

Otherwise, it would mean breaking extcaps or breaking Wireshark with extcaps that don't handle the pipes.
Does `etwdump` use non blocking reads, and is it possible for it to watch extcap_end_application or otherwise know when to shutdown?

It is blocking, and it can be shut using the `graceful_shutdown_cb` (which just calls `CloseTrace` which shuts everything down). It can even be done from another process because the trace is global for Windows, which is what the current "post-kill" hack is using
